product: Trapped-ion quantum computers. Helios is a 98-physical-qubit third-generation system commercially launched November 2025 and sold as hardware-as-a-service on-premises or in the cloud; Sol is planned for 2027 and fault-tolerant Apollo for 2029. Software includes the Nexus platform, the Guppy language, InQuanto chemistry and Quantum Origin quantum random-number generation.
demand: Early but building. More than 180 organizations now build on the Nexus platform, Q2 2026 bookings were 4.3M dollars, year-to-date bookings about 81M dollars and management targets at least 120M dollars for full year 2026, with a pipeline described as in the billions of dollars spanning Helios upgrades, Sol and Apollo engagements.
pricing_power: Limited. Adjusted gross margin was 62 percent in Q2 2026, down 60 basis points year over year, and management guides long-term gross margin only north of 50 percent. GAAP gross margin was negative 64.4 percent because of IPO-triggered stock compensation, so current pricing does not yet cover fully loaded costs.
competition: Crowded and well funded. IBM, Google, IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave and PsiQuantum pursue superconducting, annealing or photonic approaches. Quantinuum claims technology leadership after demonstrating near five-nines logical fidelity on Helios and states it is the only trapped-ion architecture recipient of CHIPS R&D funding, a claimed moat.
team: Led by President and CEO Rajeeb Hazra and CFO Nitesh Sharan, with new Head of Investor Relations Shub Mukherjee. Robin Schulman became Chief Legal Officer effective July 13 2026 and Rory O'Byrne Chief People Officer effective May 26 2026. The company carries deep Honeywell heritage plus the 2021 Cambridge Quantum Computing combination.
market_strategy: Full-stack leadership: most performant hardware plus the most widely adopted hybrid classical-quantum developer platform, delivered on-premises and via cloud through Oracle OCI, HPE and SoftBank. Leans on US government tailwinds including the 100M dollar CHIPS R&D award, CHIPS R&D Office letter of intent and June 2026 executive orders on quantum and post-quantum cryptography.
bull: Q2 2026 revenue $8M up 279% YoY, FY26 guide $28-32M, YTD bookings ~$81M vs $120M target, $2.1B cash, $100M CHIPS award finalized Sep 8 2026, Oracle Helios purchase Aug 11 2026.
bear: Revenue $8M against ~$12.9B cap; Q2 GAAP gross margin -64.4%, adjusted EPS -$0.28 miss; burn $66.2M/quarter; short interest +29.14% to 3.72M shares by Sep 15 2026; stock -25% over 63 days.
falsifier: Any company disclosure before 2027 showing FY2026 revenue below the $28M guidance floor, or a confirmed slip of the 2027 Sol launch date.
web_what_changed: IPO completed June 2026 raising 1.7B dollars gross, the first traditional IPO for a pure-play quantum company. Q2 2026 results on Aug 11 2026 showed revenue 8M dollars up 279 percent YoY and first formal FY2026 guidance of 28-32M dollars. Oracle Helios deal Aug 11, Quanta Computer manufacturing partnership Aug 13, Aramco MOU Sep 3, 100M dollar CHIPS award finalized Sep 8 2026.
web_not_known_yesterday: Not found. No company disclosure dated Sep 24 or Sep 25 2026 was located; the newest items remain the Sep 11 2026 Piper Sandler conference notice, the Sep 8 2026 CHIPS award finalization and the Sep 3 2026 Aramco MOU. Market data still reflects the Sep 24 2026 close of 49.39 dollars and Sep 15 2026 short interest.
web_demand_price_volume_mix: Volume and demand, not price. Q2 2026 revenue of 8M dollars rose 279 percent YoY driven mainly by cloud growth with roughly equal US and non-US split. Q2 bookings were 4.3M dollars, year-to-date bookings about 81M dollars, FY2026 target at least 120M dollars. Adjusted gross margin of 62 percent fell 60 basis points, so no pricing uplift.
web_suppliers: Key suppliers are GlobalFoundries for ion traps and control electronics on 300mm wafers, Monarch Quantum for lasers and optical components, Infineon Technologies and Honeywell Aerospace for critical quantum components, plus Quanta Computer and an unnamed global electronics manufacturer for at-scale manufacturing. They are constrained by novel components; the Sep 8 2026 100M dollar CHIPS R&D award aims to onshore and de-risk them.
web_customers: Concentration is low and not disclosed. Named customers and partners include Oracle, which purchased a Helios unit on Aug 11 2026, HPE, SoftBank Corp, Rolls-Royce, Quanta Computer, a Fortune 100 pharmaceutical company, NVIDIA, Aramco, plus government, national labs and universities. Management said Q2 2026 revenue was well diversified across customer type and geography.
web_who_loses: Rival quantum hardware builders in other modalities lose share if trapped-ion wins: IBM, Google, IonQ, Rigetti, D-Wave and PsiQuantum. Also pressured are classical-only HPC and cryptography vendors whose business assumes quantum advantage stays distant, and supercomputer and data-center vendors whose installed base is displaced by hybrid quantum systems.
web_contradicting_evidence: Revenue is only 8M dollars against roughly 12.9B dollars market cap. Q2 2026 adjusted EPS missed at minus 0.28 versus minus 0.26 expected and GAAP gross margin was minus 64.4 percent. Morgan Stanley rates Equal Weight with a 78 dollar target, dated Jun 29 2026; Weiss Ratings initiated at Sell Aug 31 2026. Short interest rose 29.14 percent to 3.72M shares by Sep 15 2026 and the stock is down about 25 percent over 63 days.
web_if_management_right: Sol ships in 2027 and Apollo, the first fully fault-tolerant system, launches 2029, unlocking what management calls a 10B plus dollar end-user quantum market. Own revenue reaches billions by 2030 with positive free cash flow from 2030 onward, and 2027 revenue more than doubles the 28-32M dollar 2026 guide toward 60M dollars or more.
web_if_management_wrong: Roadmap slip breaks first. Q2 2026 operating cash burn was 66.2M dollars with 16.6M dollars capex against under 32M dollars of annual revenue, so the 2.1B dollar cash pile funds only a few years. Delay of Sol 2027 or Apollo 2029 stalls bookings and revenue, forcing dilution or spending cuts, while the 62 percent adjusted gross margin compresses.
web_second_order_beneficiaries: Upstream suppliers GlobalFoundries, Monarch Quantum, Infineon and Honeywell Aerospace; manufacturing partner Quanta Computer; cloud and HPC hosts Oracle and HPE; NVIDIA for hybrid quantum-AI workloads; error-mitigation startup Qedma; laser, photonics and cryogenics vendors; national labs and universities; and sector peers such as IonQ that re-rate on QNT validation.
